guard: on a bearer REFRESH the endpoint refuses material that is already dead and material the source merely re-served, and keeps arming a short-TTL source at the 5s floor
why: Adopting a token that cannot carry the next cycle arms the next refresh from a non-positive delay,
which armBearerRefresh floors to 5s. When the source returns nothing new, the next read gets that
same token and the loop runs at 5s for its remaining life while the 15s BEARER_RETRY_MS backoff is
bypassed: the fetch did not fail, it succeeded and returned material that is not usable.
The floor itself is not the defect and must survive: expiry-renewal mints 5s bearers against the
60s margin, so for that deployment 5s IS the renewal cadence. That is why one cell counts reads
from a REFUSED source (none in 12s) and a second counts reads from a HEALTHY short-TTL source
(at least two in the same window). A change that widened the refusal into a blanket backoff would
pass the first and fail the second.
The two refusals answer different questions and are graded separately. Expiry is graded on its own
because an advance-only rule adopts a candidate dying at now-5s over a held one that died at
now-60s. Re-serve is graded on byte identity because exp carries one second of resolution, so a
key rotation re-signing the same claims, and a same-second re-read, both return NEW material whose
exp has not moved; an advancement test refuses those.
Sibling cells (the warning text, the cache staying on the last good token) cannot grade any of this
alone: a future change could emit the message, or leave the cache alone, and still re-read at the

mutations.name: an expired candidate is adopted when it advances the held one
mutations.expectRed: an expired candidate is refused even though it ADVANCES the held one
mutations.cell: an expired candidate is refused even though it ADVANCES the held one
mutations.note: This reinstates the exact rule review rejected rather than deleting the guard, so the cell fails only for the reason it exists. A deleted guard also reds this cell, but so would any change that stops the refusal firing at all; making the refusal conditional on NOT advancing keeps it armed for every other expired token.

mutations.name: the re-serve test goes back to an advancement comparison
mutations.expectRed: a re-signed token carrying the same exp IS adopted
mutations.cell: a re-signed token carrying the same exp IS adopted
mutations.note: The false refusal that advancement produces, and the reason the shipped test is byte identity. A token re-signed under a rotated key carries the same exp, so an advancement test calls it stale and backs off 15s against material the broker has just started requiring.

mutations.name: a non-positive delay is clamped to BEARER_RETRY_MS
mutations.replace: const d = expiryMs - Date.now() - CotalEndpoint.BEARER_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS; this.armBearerRefresh(d <= 0 ? CotalEndpoint.BEARER_RETRY_MS : d);
mutations.expectRed: a healthy short-TTL source still renews at the floor (>= 2 reads in 12s)
mutations.cell: a healthy short-TTL source still renews at the floor (>= 2 reads in 12s)
mutations.note: Backing every inside-margin token off to the failure cadence looks like a fix for the loop and is not: a deployment whose whole TTL sits inside the margin then holds a dead token for two thirds of every cycle. This mutation is the reason the loop is closed at the source test instead of the timer.

mutations.name: both refusals are applied with no token held
mutations.expectRed: the initial fetch is adopted even when it is already expired
mutations.cell: the initial fetch is adopted even when it is already expired
mutations.note: Both refusals protect a cached token, so with no cache there is nothing to protect and start() has to come up on whatever the source has. bindConnection's pre-dial guard is what speaks for a dead first token, and it names the remedy; refusing here instead leaves the endpoint with no bearer at all and the authenticator presenting undefined.
